title: Appfire Flow to Waydev, the easy way
summary: Practical 2027 Appfire Flow migration checklist: export reports, map metrics and teams, and evaluate Waydev Brain, Signals and dashboards.
body_markdown:
**2027 enterprise migration guide · updated October 2026**


## Why move from Appfire Flow to Waydev Brain?


When replacing a legacy engineering intelligence system, preserve your history, team identities and reporting definitions first. Then evaluate whether the new intelligence layer supports private AI analysis, proactive alerts and flexible reporting.


### Proprietary Waydev 30B and air-gapped deployment


Waydev Brain uses Waydev’s proprietary 30-billion-parameter SDLC model. A fully air-gapped deployment option supports organizations that require engineering intelligence within their own environment. Confirm infrastructure, data handling and access requirements in a security review.


### Agents, Signals, AI Goals and Prompt Dashboards


[Waydev Agent](https://waydev.co/features/waydev-agent/) can answer questions over connected engineering data.[Signals](https://waydev.co/features/signals/) surface delivery changes;[AI-suggested Goals](https://waydev.co/features/goals/) track objectives;[Prompt Dashboards](https://waydev.co/features/prompt-dashboards/) assemble editable reporting from natural-language prompts. AI Adoption, Impact and ROI help assess the outcomes and cost of AI-assisted work.


Waydev product visualExisting Waydev feature graphic


### A migration plan that protects historical reporting


1. Export Flow dashboards and historical metrics before the end of service.
2. Verify Git and issue-tracker connectors, team identities and metric definitions.
3. Compare Waydev dashboards with a parallel baseline on matching repositories.
4. Test private Brain deployment, Signals and organization permissions before cutover.


Compare migration approaches in the[related Waydev guide](https://waydev.co/migrating-from-appfire-flow-a-practical-guide-for-engineering-teams/) . **Waydev pricing is private** , with commercial terms discussed directly with enterprise buyers.[Request a Waydev Brain migration demo](https://waydev.co/demo/) .


Product and deployment claims follow Waydev’s published feature descriptions; specific migration assistance and historical-data availability must be confirmed for each customer.


## Before anything else: export your Flow history


Do this first, before you take a single demo, including ours. Flow holds years of engineering history that nobody else has: cycle time trends, review patterns, commit level baselines, and the dashboard definitions someone on your team spent two quarters tuning.


Pull the following out of Flow while your account is still live:


- Raw metric exports from Team health insights, Review collaboration, Retrospective, and Work log, at team and org level, for the longest window your plan allows
- Ticket log and Deployment log exports, since these carry your DORA baselines
- Screenshots or written definitions of every custom dashboard, saved filter, and report configuration. The data is recoverable. The reasoning behind a bespoke dashboard usually is not, especially if the person who built it has left
- Your team structure: team names, membership, and the developer alias and identity mappings Flow built up over the years
- Your ticket project configurations, including which Jira statuses count as Done and which are excluded


Then ask every vendor you evaluate one question: can you ingest this, or do we start from zero?
